subject.title: feat(gateway): pre-handshake WS verifyClient with Sec-Fetch-Site and forwarded-header hardening

question: Should Gateway adopt this pre-upgrade hardening as opt-in policy in the HTTP upgrade owner, or intentionally make any forwarded/protocol checks default-on?
rationale: The answer defines a public security and compatibility boundary, three configuration settings, and whether existing proxy traffic may start failing without operator action; code review cannot choose that policy safely.

options.title: Use an opt-in upgrade gate
options.body: Move validation into the HTTP upgrade handler, inspect raw header lines, and require an approved setting for every newly introduced rejection.

options.title: Approve default-on checks
options.body: Keep selected forwarded/protocol checks default-on only with explicit compatibility acceptance, upgrade documentation, and representative proxy proof.

options.title: Narrow the proposal
options.body: Limit this PR to raw duplicate-header hardening or another independently approved subset and defer the broader policy surface.

recommendation.title: Use an opt-in upgrade gate
recommendation.body: Move validation into the HTTP upgrade handler, inspect raw header lines, and require an approved setting for every newly introduced rejection.

likelyOwner.reason: The discussion explicitly requests steipete's decision on gate placement and setting names, and the adjacent Gateway origin boundary follows work merged under that direction.
